ratings_why.fun: One visible number that you vote every turn, plus a slot puzzle of floaters and Dikes, gives each turn a real choice and plenty of permanent growth to watch.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7: the Level is a public dial that hurts both front rows before anyone attacks, so where you put coots and beavers matters more than stats, and no tribe today works like that.

verdict_why: The core reads well and fits the theme, but what counts as one Raise or Drain needs defining before the trigger cards can be read the same way by everyone.

points.text: "Whenever you Raise" and "Whenever you Drain" don't say whether Raise 2 fires once or twice, or whether a Raise blocked at 5 still counts. Ring-Dike Beaver, Ditch-Digger, Master of the Nine Mills and Hendrika all depend on this, so define it once, for example as one trigger per step that moves.
Kees Kowk says "After the Flood", but a fight can have your Flood, the enemy's Flood and Tail-Slapper's repeats. Say "After each Flood" or "After your Flood".
Show the Flood as a water line on each front-row card, marking the Health it will lose at the current Level, so nobody has to work out tenths.
Objecting Coot raising the Level when you sell is a loose fit. Coots object to boundary lines, so an objection when a unit moves next to it or is played beside it would carry the joke better.
Hendrika's text is long for a capstone. "Twice a turn, when you Raise or Drain, you may carry it all the way to 5 or 0" says the same thing.

standouts.why: The Spaarndam Pup plugging the dike so your Floods only drown the enemy is the seed's story in one clear line.
Ring-Dike Beaver shows the slot puzzle at Tier 2: keep its neighbours dry and grow them on every Raise.
Polder Millwright raising and draining every turn is the swinging water board in miniature, and it reads at a glance.

weakest.why: Objecting Coot's sell trigger has little to do with objecting or with water.
Inspecting Heemraad feeds only the diagonal slots and does nothing in the front row, which players will often get wrong.
Hendrika's wording is the hardest card to parse, and how her extra steps interact with the Raise and Drain triggers is unclear.

flags.note: Hendrika with Kobus Bles and Old Bram or the Nine Mills gives ten or more doubled changes a turn, a big high roll worth the owner's eye.
Tail-Slapper's repeat Floods, combined with The Spaarndam Pup, could wipe both enemy rows before many attacks happen.
Whether a Raise of 2, or a Raise blocked at 5, fires "Whenever you Raise" is not defined; the same goes for Ditch-Digger and the Nine Mills on Drains.
"After the Flood" doesn't say which Flood when both players and Tail-Slapper flood.
